taxon: Simulium tani; Simulium suoivangense; Simulium xuandei
character: Species complex boundaries and cryptic taxa
value_a: COI/COII fail to resolve S. tani complex; nuclear ECP1 + concatenated dataset validate cytoform K (= S. tani s.s., Malaysia) and morphoform 'b' (= cytoform M, later S. suoivangense, Vietnam), reveal possible cryptic species in S. xuandei (1-2), cytoform L (Taiwan) and morphoform 'a' (Vietnam), and treat Thai cytoforms A, C, G as incomplete lineage sorting with cytoform B in early reproductive isolation
value_b: Chromosomes resolve 4 Vietnamese cytoforms (B2, M, N, S. xuandei); B2 and N occur sympatrically in morphoform 'a' with 3 fixed-inversion differences and no hybrids (reproductively isolated), whereas S. xuandei shows 1 chromosomal species in 9 larvae
comment: Putt et al. (2023) also report non-monophyly of COI among S. tani complex (up to 5.94% divergence), S. suoivangense and S. xuandei; nuclear ECP1 and chromosomes are needed for reliable delimitation.

value_b: Morphologically separated by coloration of female hind tibia and basitarsus; nuclear ECP1 separates the two complexes
comment: Putt et al. (2023) likewise show non-monophyly in the S. tuberosum group based on COI alone.

taxon: Simulium doipuiense; Simulium rosliramlii; Simulium rufibasis

value_b: COI shows non-monophyly and 0.74% minimum interspecific distance between S. doipuiense complex (intraspecific up to 7.92%) and S. rosliramlii (intraspecific up to 8.17%), likely due to introgression or incomplete lineage sorting

taxon: Simulium asakoae; Simulium chaudinhense; Simulium hongthaii; Simulium vinhphucense
character: Cryptic diversity and COI/BZF barcoding limitations
value_a: Morphologically identified Thai 'S. asakoae' females split into 3 (ASAP/PTP) to 4 (GMYC) COI MOTUs (max K2P 7.92%), matching S. asakoae, S. nanthaburiense, S. chaowaense, S. pitasawatae, S. tamdaoense/S. myanmarense, S. vinhphucense and S. hongthaii
value_b: All 8 Vietnamese S. asakoae group species are non-monophyletic in COI; COI+BZF recovers S. asakoae s.str. as weakly monophyletic, while Aupalee et al. (2026) confirm multiplex PCR separates Thai S. asakoae with 100% specificity but may cross-react with Vietnamese S. chaudinhense, S. hongthaii and S. vinhphucense
comment: Females of the S. asakoae group cannot be reliably separated by morphology or COI alone; nuclear markers beyond BZF or region-validated multiplex PCR are required.

value_b: S. phami and S. pumatense are morphologically distinct in larval labral fan rays, pupal gill filament number, male upper-eye facets and female cibarial conical processes
comment: COI has insufficient phylogenetic signal to separate closely related members of the S. feuerborni group.

value_a: S. daoense paratypes (OQ117837-OQ117840) and GenBank topotypes (MG734007-MG734009) differ by up to 15.10% COI p-distance, with the latter clustering inside the S. striatum group; S. lacduongense, S. laui and S. ubonae share 0.00-0.25% COI distance
value_b: Morphologically S. lacduongense has a haired basal radial vein in females (bare in S. laui and S. ubonae), and all three differ in male upper-eye facets and ovipositor valve inner margins
comment: COI is ineffective in the S. multistriatum group; ECP1 is recommended, and S. daoense topotype GenBank sequences (MG734007-MG734009) require verification for possible misidentification or cryptic species.
